## Introduction

This script implements a hierarchical testing procedure applied across the 
primary and key secondary endpoints to control the family-wise type I error 
rate. Endpoints are tested sequentially in a predefined order (cf. the Statistical
Analysis Plan). An endpoint is considered significant only if it meets the 
significance criterion and all preceding endpoints in the sequence were also 
significant.


## Hierarchical testing procedure

Get metadata registry
```{r}
tlf_reg <- get_metadata()
```

Define the ordered set of outcome specifications corresponding to the testing hierarchy 
```{r}
idx <- data.table(
  outcome_var = c(rep("madrs_total10", 6), rep("hamd_total17",2),
                  rep("mdi_total",2), "eq5d5l_scale", "madrs_total10"),
  outcome_type = c(rep("cont", 4), rep("binary", 2), rep("cont", 5), "binary"),
  outcome_kind = c(rep("chgbl", 4), "responder", "remission", rep("chgbl", 5), 
                   "sustain"),
  visit = c(7, 4, 14, 28, 7, 7, 7, 28, 7, 28, 7, 28),
  estimand = "policy",
  tlf_type = "table",
  role = "Primary",
  `Test order` = 1:12
  )
idx
```

Look up expected counts for remission, repsonder and sustained response analyses,
and modify outcome specification if expected counts are <5 or data exhibits 
complete separation.
```{r}
# Meta data rows for summary of responder, remission and sustained response 
# on MADRS-10 total (policy estimand)
bin_reg <- tlf_reg[outcome_var == "madrs_total10" &
                     estimand == "policy" &
                     role == "Summary" &
                     outcome_type == "binary"]

#' Get expected and minimum observed counts for a binary endpoint
#'
#' For a single endpoint defined by a metadata row, extracts the number of
#' cases at the relevant visit and computes the expected count and the number 
#' of cases in the arm with the fewest cases.
#'
#' The visit is chosen according to the outcome kind: Day 28 for sustained
#' response and Day 7 for responder and remission.
#'
#' @param regi A one-row `data.table` with metadata for the endpoint Must
#'   contain the column `outcome_kind` with one of the values `"sustain"`,
#'   `"responder"` or `"remission"`.
#'
#' @return A one-row `data.table` with columns `outcome_kind` (the outcome kind 
#' taken from `regi`),`N_expected` (expected number of cases per arm), and `N_min`
#' (the number of cases in the arm with the fewest cases).
#' 
get_expected_counts <- function(regi){
  # check outcome_kind is sustained response, responder or remission
  stopifnot(nrow(regi) == 1,
            regi$outcome_kind %in% c("sustain","responder","remission"))
  
  # set visit to day 7 for responder and remission and day 28 for sustained response
  visit <- fifelse(regi$outcome_kind == "sustain", "day28", "day7")
  
  # get dt table based on meta data row
  tab <- get_dt_table(regi)
  
  # Identify which outcome_kind column is present in this table and rename to 
  # N_obs
  tab[, outcome_kind := regi$outcome_kind]
  n_col <- intersect(names(tab), c("Responder", "Remission", "Sustained response"))
  stopifnot(length(n_col) == 1)
  setnames(tab, n_col, "N_obs")
  
  # Extract relevant rows and columns
  cols <- c("trt","f_visit", "outcome_kind", "N_obs")
  rows <- tab[f_visit == visit, .SD, .SDcols = cols]
  
  # Compute expected counts and number of cases in the arm with least cases
  N_expected <- rows[trt == "Any treatment",  N_obs/2]
  N_min <- rows[trt != "Any treatment", min(N_obs)]
  
  # Return:
  data.table(outcome_kind = regi[, outcome_kind],
             N_expected = N_expected,
             N_min = N_min)
}

# Calculate expected counts for binary outcomes
bin_exp_count <- rbindlist(lapply(1:nrow(bin_reg), function(i) get_expected_counts(bin_reg[i])))
bin_exp_count

# Modify idx for binary outcomes with expected counts <5 or complete separation
idx[outcome_kind %in% bin_exp_count[N_expected < 5 | N_min == 0]$outcome_kind, 
    role := "Unconditional exact"]
idx
```

Select the metadata rows corresponding to the primary and key secondary outcomes
```{r}
# Select the metadata rows
th_reg <- tlf_reg[idx, on = setdiff(names(idx), "Test order"), mult = "all"]
setorder(th_reg, `Test order`)

# Ensure correct number of rows and only primary and key secondary endpoints are 
# included
stopifnot(nrow(idx) == 12,
          nrow(th_reg) == nrow(idx),
          th_reg[, unique(endpoint_level)] %in% c("Primary", "Key secondary")
          )
```

Extract stats from tables included in the book based on metadata
```{r}
#' Append metadata rows for primary and secondary endpoints with results from 
#' the table corresponding to the row's endpoint_id 
#'
#' @param regi A one-row `data.table` with metadata for the endpoint. 
#'
#' @return A one-row `data.table` where the metadata row has been appended with
#' the following statistics: 
#' * `estimate`: The treatment effect estimate (OR for binary endpoints, ETD
#'    for continuous endpoints)
#' * `lower.CL`, `upper.CL`: Lower and upper confidence limits for `estimate`, 
#' * `Effect`: The formatted treatment effect with confidence interval
#' * `p-value`: p-value for the test of no treatment effect
#' * `Dexamethasone`, `Placebo`: Estimated mean for each treatment arm (continuous
#'    endpoints) or number of cases/subjects included (binary endpoints)
#' 
get_stats <- function(reg){
  
  # Function adding stats to one row
  get_stats_one_row <- function(i, reg){
    # Select meta data row number i
    regi <- reg[i]
    
    # Get dt table
    tab <- get_dt_table(regi)
    
    # Select relevant rows based on visit
    rows <- tab[Visit == paste("Day", regi$visit)]
    
    # Get treatment names
    trt_levels <- unique(as.character(rows$trt))
    dexa <- grep("[Dd]exa", trt_levels, value = TRUE)
    placebo <- grep("[Pp]lacebo", trt_levels, value = TRUE)
    
    stopifnot(
      length(dexa) == 1,
      length(placebo) == 1,
      dexa != placebo
    )
    
    # Mark whether analysis is binary
    is_binary <- regi[, outcome_type == "binary"]
    
    # Mark whether analysis is unconditional exact test
    is_uce <- regi[, role == "Unconditional exact"]
    
    # Define columns where single value should be extracted depending on
    # outcome and analysis type
    cols <- if (is_binary & !is_uce) {
      c(Effect = "OR (95% CI)", estimate = "odds.ratio",
        lower.CL = "lwr.lrt", upper.CL = "upr.lrt")
    } else if (is_binary & is_uce){
      c(Effect = "OR (95% CI)", estimate = "odds.ratio",
        lower.CL = "lwr_ci", upper.CL = "upr_ci")
    } else {
      c(Effect = "Effect (95% CI)", estimate = "estimate",
        lower.CL = "lower.CL", upper.CL = "upper.CL")
    }
    
    # Append p-value column to cols
    cols <- c(cols, `p-value` = "p-value")
    
    # Define column for estimated means/counts depending on outcome and 
    # analysis type
    est_col <- if (is_binary) regi[, oc_kind_label] else "Est. Mean (95% CI)"
    stopifnot(
      length(est_col) == 1 && !is.na(est_col),
      est_col %in% names(rows)
    )
    
    # Function extracting a single non-NA value
    get_value <- function(x) {
      x <- x[!is.na(x)]
      stopifnot(length(x) == 1)
      x
    }
    # Collect values in the desired column order
    vals <- c(
      setNames(list(rows[trt == dexa][[est_col]],
                    rows[trt == placebo][[est_col]]),
               c(dexa, placebo)),
      lapply(cols, function(col) get_value(rows[[col]]))
    )
    
    # Add columns to regi
    regi[, names(vals) := vals]

    # Return
    regi
  }
  
  # Run get stats for all rows in reg 
  res <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(reg)), get_stats_one_row, reg = reg))
  
  # Return
  res
}

th_reg <- get_stats(th_reg)
```

Apply hierarchical test procedure to control for multiple testing
```{r}
# Flag whether a test favors Dexamethasone
th_reg[, favors_dexa := fifelse(
  fcase(
    outcome_type == "binary", estimate > 1,
    outcome_var  == "eq5d5l_scale",     estimate > 0,
    default = estimate < 0
  ),
  "yes", "no"
)]

# Flag Superiority if test is significant (alpha = 0.05) and favors Dexamethasone
th_reg[, Superiority := ifelse(`p-value` < 0.05 & favors_dexa == "yes", "Yes", "No")]

# Apply the hierarchical testing procedure, i.e. once a test is non-significant, 
# all subsequent tests are considered non-significant
th_reg[, `p-value` := replace(`p-value`, cumsum(Superiority == "No") > 1, "Not tested")]
th_reg[, Superiority := replace(Superiority, cumsum(Superiority == "No") > 0, "No")]
```

Format table for presentation
```{r}
# Format outcome
th_reg[outcome_type == "cont", Outcome := paste("Change in", variable_label, "at Day", visit)]
th_reg[outcome_kind == "responder", Outcome := paste0(outcome_label, " at Day ", visit, "†")]
th_reg[outcome_kind == "remission", Outcome := paste0(outcome_label, " at Day ", visit, "‡")]
th_reg[outcome_kind == "sustain", Outcome := paste0(outcome_label, " at Day ", visit, "§")]
th_reg[, Outcome := gsub("Responder", "Response", Outcome)]

# Save data.table object
saveRDS(th_reg, "50_output_db/outputs/summary_primary_key_secondary_analyses.rds")

# Select columns
th_dt <- th_reg[, .(Outcome, `Test order`, `p-value`, Superiority, endpoint_id)]

# Add source
th_dt[, `Source table` := paste0("[-@sec-", endpoint_id, "]")]

# Convert to a gt table
th_gt <- gt(th_dt[, !"endpoint_id"]) |> set_gt_style() |>
  cols_align(
    align = "left",
    columns = Outcome
  ) 
```

Attach footers and display final table
```{r}
# Get footer metadata
footers <- get_footers()

# Define footers
th_footer <- list(definition = paste("Superiority is claimed if all preceding endpoints in the hierarchy",
                                     "have met the significance criteria and the effects favor dexamethasone. ", 
                                     "All analyses address the primary estimand (treatment policy).",
                                     "All analyses use the Full Analysis Set (FAS).",
                                     "For binary endpoints, if the expected counts are below 5 or data exhibit",
                                     "complete separation, the p-value is obtained from an unconditional exact",
                                     "test, as prespecified in the SAP."),
                  scale = paste(footers[type == "scale" & key %in% c("MADRS~10~", "ANCOVA", "HAM-D~17~",
                                                                     "MDI","EQ-5D-5L Visual-Analogue Scale"), 
                                        footer], collapse = ". "),
                  abbrev = c("† A responder is defined by the MADRS~10~ score being reduced by at least 50% from baseline (day 0).",
                             "‡ Remission is defined by a MADRS~10~ score ≤ 10.",
                             "§ Sustained response is defined by the response score being reduced by at least 50% from baseline (day 0) at all visits from Day 7 up to and including Day 28.")
                  )

# Attach footers to gt table
th_gt <- add_footer_lines_to_gt(th_gt, th_footer)

# Display result
th_gt
```

Save gt table
```{r}
save_gt_table(th_gt, 
              regi = tlf_reg[file_stem == "hierarchical_testing_results"], 
              verbose = TRUE)
```
